candidates.falsification_check: Reject if the held-out CSS family lacks a short expert construction, if any fault class is underspecified, or if the TensorCircuit execution is only a wrapper around a classical tableau answer.
candidates.novelty_note: Directly fills the QEC/fault-tolerant-synthesis roadmap gap; StabilizerBench reports substantial headroom across three frontier agents, none of which was GPT-5.6-sol.
candidates.objective: Synthesize a CSS logical-state preparation and verification circuit that preserves the target stabilizers and detects every declared low-weight propagated fault.
candidates.oracle_design: Polynomial stabilizer/isometry checks plus exhaustive single-fault propagation and exact small-code state verification.
review_questions: Which held-out CSS codes have short expert circuits?
Are all injected fault locations and acceptance rules explicit?
Does exhaustive fault enumeration remain below the verifier budget?

candidates.title: Fault-tolerant CSS state-preparation synthesis
candidates.why_plausibly_hard: Requires constructive stabilizer reasoning, verification-circuit synthesis, propagation analysis, and exact fault-tolerance semantics; this is supported by direct agent-benchmark evidence rather than size alone.

candidates.falsification_check: Reject if the pinned FGS API cannot reproduce exact small-system correlators and gradients with fixed ordering conventions.
candidates.novelty_note: Adds specialized fermionic simulation and conditional Gaussian measurement, absent from tasks 01-12.
candidates.objective: Evolve a Kitaev-chain Gaussian state, condition on occupation outcomes, and recover parity correlators or hidden quench parameters.
candidates.oracle_design: Exact Jordan-Wigner simulation on tiny instances plus an independent covariance-matrix implementation on production instances.
review_questions: Is the FGS API stable in the pinned image?
Can parity and occupation ordering be specified without ambiguity?
Does the dense oracle remain independent?

candidates.tensorcircuit_path: Use TensorCircuit's FGS covariance engine for Bogoliubov evolution, measurement conditioning, and parity observables; forbid dense Jordan-Wigner statevectors at production scale.
candidates.title: Conditioned fermionic-Gaussian Kitaev quench
candidates.why_plausibly_hard: Requires translating BdG/covariance conventions into an unfamiliar specialized API, then composing measurement conditioning with inverse validation.

candidates.falsification_check: Require a fixed nullspace, a lower bound on every nonzero support eigenvalue, and agreement between AD and finite-difference QFIMs before any solver trial.
candidates.novelty_note: Adds multiparameter information geometry and rank-aware mixed-state optimization, unlike current energy/fidelity objectives.
candidates.objective: Optimize a noisy probe circuit using the symmetric-logarithmic-derivative quantum Fisher information matrix on a fixed support whose nonzero eigenvalues obey an explicit lower bound.
candidates.oracle_design: Finite-difference density derivatives and an independent eigenbasis SLD implementation with hidden parameter points.
review_questions: Is the density-matrix support fixed over the full parameter domain?
Are SLD and parameter-order conventions explicit?
Is the target reachable without optimizer luck?

candidates.why_plausibly_hard: Combines noisy circuit AD, complex-valued Jacobian conventions, support-restricted spectral formulas, and a non-scalar design objective.

candidates.falsification_check: Reject targets whose phase solution is unreachable, ill-conditioned, or dominated by an external classical package.
candidates.novelty_note: Adds constructive fault-tolerant-era algorithm synthesis instead of NISQ variational physics.
candidates.objective: Recover parity-constrained phase factors for a hidden target polynomial and verify the resulting TensorCircuit QSP response on an independent grid.
candidates.oracle_design: Independent polynomial evaluation, unitarity/parity identities, and dense response checks on hidden grid points.
review_questions: Does TensorCircuit remain central rather than a final wrapper?
Is the phase gauge fixed?
Do hidden grid checks prevent polynomial hard-coding?

candidates.tensorcircuit_path: Implement the QSP SU(2) sequence as a parameterized TensorCircuit and use backend AD to fit phase factors under fixed gauge conventions.
candidates.title: Quantum signal-processing phase synthesis
candidates.why_plausibly_hard: Requires mapping polynomial parity and gauge constraints to a numerically stable phase parameterization, not merely composing familiar gates.

candidates.falsification_check: Reject unless pinned-image canaries cover reset, zero-probability branches, normalization, and classical feed-forward, or if the verifier averages away branch-specific errors.
candidates.novelty_note: Adds semantic verification of adaptive circuits rather than another feedback-control objective.
candidates.objective: Given two measurement-conditioned circuits with resets and feed-forward, construct a branch-sensitive certificate or counterexample showing whether their induced quantum instruments agree.
candidates.oracle_design: Independent branchwise Choi matrices, trace-preservation identities, and planted inequivalent mutations with exact witnesses.
review_questions: Are zero-probability branches handled explicitly?
Can mutations isolate reset, normalization, and feed-forward failures?
Is TensorCircuit doing substantive branch execution?

candidates.title: Dynamic-circuit branch equivalence certificate
candidates.why_plausibly_hard: Ordinary unitary equivalence is insufficient: the solver must preserve measurement probabilities, normalized conditional states, reset semantics, and later feed-forward across all reachable branches.

candidates.falsification_check: Plant a known spectral gap and reject instances whose target eigenpairs are not stable across a declared regularization interval.

candidates.oracle_design: Exact eigenspectrum and subspace residual checks.
review_questions: Is the conditioning range difficult but numerically identifiable?
Are basis gauge and truncation rules explicit?
Do residual checks prevent simply returning exact reference energies?

Can held-out predictions be verified deterministically?

candidates.title: Variance-aware circuit cutting reconstruction
candidates.why_plausibly_hard: The task couples quantum subcircuit construction to signed quasiprobability recombination and variance allocation; local correctness does not guarantee an unbiased global estimate.

candidates.falsification_check: Reject if the pinned image lacks a stable differentiable propagator, the expert cannot meet the runtime gate, or random restarts dominate the outcome.

review_questions: Are amplitude, bandwidth, and leakage conventions complete?
Can hidden ensemble members test robustness without optimizer lottery?
Does the independent propagator agree at every gate boundary?

candidates.tensorcircuit_path: Use TensorCircuit qudit/custom-gate primitives with Diffrax/JAX evolution and automatic differentiation.
candidates.title: Leakage-aware robust GRAPE control
candidates.why_plausibly_hard: The solver must reconcile qutrit leakage, differentiable time evolution, control constraints, and worst-case ensemble performance; a pulse that works only at the nominal Hamiltonian is insufficient.

candidates.falsification_check: Reject instances whose graph structure makes every contraction exponential under the cap or whose reference plan relies on an unpinned private optimizer.
candidates.novelty_note: Turns scalable simulation into a constructive planning problem with a checkable scientific output, complementing representation-only tasks 08-10.
candidates.objective: Plan and execute a tensor-network contraction for a structured nonlocal circuit under an explicit peak-memory budget, returning selected amplitudes and contraction-cost evidence.
candidates.oracle_design: Exact amplitudes on reduced circuits, independently contracted production amplitudes, and measured peak-memory/cost checks for the submitted plan.
review_questions: Is the accepted plan feasible on the actual Docker memory limit?
Can peak memory be measured reproducibly?
Do hidden amplitudes prevent hard-coded outputs while remaining independently checkable?
